tasks.title: PanelBar carries open state on aria-current, not aria-pressed (E3)
acceptance: The per-panel button in `src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.tsx` (the `aria-pressed={open === key}` at `:83` at `41f274e` — re-grep rather than trusting the line number) sets `aria-current` instead, so the open panel's button exposes `aria-current="true"` and no other panel button exposes `aria-current="true"`. Evidence: `grep -n "aria-pressed=" src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.tsx` exits 1; positive-controlled by `grep -n "aria-current" src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.tsx` exiting 0. The first grep exits 0 at this task's startRef, so the criterion is not vacuous.

`src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.module.css`'s open-state rule (`.button[aria-pressed='true']` at `:43` at `41f274e`) selects on the new attribute instead, and the file carries no `[aria-pressed` selector. Evidence: `grep -n "\[aria-pressed" src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.module.css` exits 1; positive control `grep -n "\[aria-current" src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.module.css` exits 0.

`src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.test.tsx` reads no `aria-pressed` attribute in any assertion. Evidence: `grep -n "'aria-pressed'" src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.test.tsx` exits 1; positive control with `'aria-current'` exits 0. Prose mentioning the rejected attribute in a comment is permitted; an assertion on it is not.

PRESERVED BEHAVIOUR — stated as such and therefore exempt from the vacuity rule. `aria-pressed` is correct on the genuine two-state toggles and must survive untouched. Evidence: after the change, `grep -rl "aria-pressed" src/renderer/src` still lists all seven of `transcript/TranscriptFilterToggle.tsx`, `transcript/Transcript.module.css`, `transcript/TranscriptPane.filter.test.tsx`, `lanes/LaneRow.tsx`, `lanes/LaneRail.test.tsx`, `__tests__/panes.e2e.test.tsx`, `__tests__/wording.e2e.test.tsx`. None of them is in this task's ownership set, so none may appear in its diff.

The rationale docblock in `PanelBar.tsx` whose paragraph began `OPEN STATE IS NOT CARRIED BY COLOUR. \`aria-pressed\` says it, and ...` (`:31` at `41f274e`) names the attribute that now says it, and records why the toggle attribute was wrong here: `aria-current` indicates the current item within a set of related elements, while `aria-pressed` is for a toggle button with two reachable states, and this button has one because the frozen contract makes a re-click on the open panel's own button a no-op. Evidence: `grep -n "says it" src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.tsx` returns exactly one line (`:31` at startRef) and that line names `aria-current`; the same command at startRef returns a line naming `aria-pressed`. The sentence must move with the attribute: prose outliving the code it described is this project's most repeated defect class.

`PanelBar.module.css`'s header paragraph (`Open state is carried by \`aria-pressed\`, and the selector below hangs off that attribute rather than off a class ...`, `:8-11` at `41f274e`) names the new attribute and keeps its argument intact: the state is expressed once, in the accessibility tree, and the colour merely follows it, so there is no way to paint a button open without also announcing it. This is the frontend discipline's accessibility floor — `Color is never the only carrier of meaning` — and it is load-bearing for this change, not decoration.

The protected test case at `PanelBar.test.tsx:50-59` at `41f274e`, named `'carries the open state on aria-pressed, not on colour alone'` and deliberately protected by sub-session C1's criterion 11, is edited UNDER THE SANCTION OF ESCALATION E3 and still asserts that open state is carried non-visually: it reads the ARIA attribute off the open panel's button and off a closed panel's button, and distinguishes them. Its name states the attribute it now checks and claims no more than its assertions check (test discipline: `The name must not claim more than the test checks`), and the name no longer contains the string `aria-pressed`.

`npx vitest run src/renderer/src/shell/PanelBar.test.tsx src/renderer/src/shell/Panels.styles.test.ts src/renderer/src/shell/App.smoke.test.tsx src/renderer/src/shell/panel-close-guard.test.tsx` passes with 0 failures. The report names that command and names the failure observed from the edited test case BEFORE the component and stylesheet changes landed — a test never seen failing has not been shown to test anything. Suite-wide numbers are deliberately NOT asserted here: this task runs concurrently with peers holding uncommitted work, and a repo-wide run on a non-quiescent tree reports phantom failures. T3 is the DAG tail and carries those.

tasks.title: Record the whole-state reset and the criterion-6 reading in prose (E4 + item 5)
acceptance: The `incoming` docblock in `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-panels.ts` (the four-event clearing list declared `EXHAUSTIVE — an event not named here leaves \`incoming\` alone` at `:406-411` at `41f274e` — re-grep rather than trusting the line numbers) names a FIFTH clearing event: the panel-close whole-state reset, in which `resetHelmForReopen` replaces the whole Helm state via `newHelmState(null)` when `helmMounts` reaches 0, so `incoming` goes null alongside `document` and `draft`. The word `EXHAUSTIVE` stays and is now true. Evidence: `grep -n "resetHelmForReopen" src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-panels.ts` exits 0, and exits 1 at this task's startRef.

That fifth entry is stamped with this session's slug using the convention the file already uses — `ADDED by session \`<slug>\`` (see `:400` and `:427` at `41f274e`). Evidence: `grep -n "ADDED by session" src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-panels.ts` returns a line naming `2026-10-09-orcastrate-theme-contract-decisions`, and no such line exists at startRef.

The `resetHelmForReopen` docblock in `src/renderer/src/state/panel-store.ts` — `Closing Helm drops the loaded document and any unsaved draft with it` at `:328` at `41f274e`, which has the identical hole one line from the code — also names `incoming`, and says it goes null as part of the whole-state replacement rather than through a targeted clear. Evidence: `grep -B4 "private resetHelmForReopen" src/renderer/src/state/panel-store.ts | grep -c incoming` returns at least 1, and returns 0 at startRef.

NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE — stated as such and therefore exempt from the vacuity rule. The behaviour at `panel-store.ts:329-331` is CORRECT; only the prose describing it was false. Every edit this task makes to `renderer-panels.ts` and `panel-store.ts` sits inside a comment or a docblock, and the task's diff contains no change to any executable statement, type, signature or exported value. The reviewer verifies this on the diff.

`src/renderer/src/helm/HelmPanel.tsx`'s docblock above the `draft === null ? null : <HelmComparison .../>` gate (`:118-124` at `41f274e`) records WHICH reading of sub-session C1's T4 criterion 6 governs, since the criterion's letter admits two: the frontend discipline rule the criterion transcribed — `Every fetch has a declared loading state, a declared error state, and a declared empty state` — governs the states OF A FETCH, not whether the surface mounts before any fetch is possible; `HelmComparison` declares all three whenever a draft exists; with no scope chosen there is no fetch, no pending edit and no file; and `draft === null && incoming !== null` is unreachable, as C1's reviewer separately established. Evidence: the docblock contains both the string `criterion 6` and the word `unreachable`; `grep -n "criterion 6" src/renderer/src/helm/HelmPanel.tsx` and `grep -n "unreachable" src/renderer/src/helm/HelmPanel.tsx` each exit 0, and each exits 1 at startRef. This is why the criterion is not vacuous: the existing docblock argues the conclusion but names neither the criterion, nor the discipline rule it transcribed, nor the unreachability finding.

THE GATING IS UNCHANGED. `HelmPanel.tsx`'s `draft === null` condition on the comparison surface, and the `draft === null` branch that renders `COPY.scopeUnchosen`, are byte-identical to startRef. This is a prose-only deliverable; a reviewer finding a changed condition here should treat it as blocking.

`.dir-sdlc/sessions/2026-08-31-orcastrate-helm-draft-safety/contracts/helm-draft-safety.ts:142` is UNTOUCHED. It carries the same four-event clearing list, it is a frozen artifact of a merged session, and this project never edits those. It is outside this task's ownership set and must not appear in its diff.

`npx vitest run src/renderer/src/state src/renderer/src/helm src/renderer/src/contracts` passes with 0 failures. The report names the command and its result. tasks.title: Semibold and overlay tokens: amend the theme contract, convert the 19 sites, release the pin (E1 + E2)
acceptance: `TOKENS` in `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-theme.ts` gains exactly two keys, ADDITIONS ONLY, under a new amendment comment stamped with this session's slug `2026-10-09-orcastrate-theme-contract-decisions`, in the style of the two amendment blocks the file already carries (`:82-86` and `:140-148` at `41f274e`): `weightSemibold: '--oc-weight-semibold'` and `overlayScrim: '--oc-overlay-scrim'`. Nothing above is renamed, revalued, removed or reordered, so no existing component's appearance changes as a side effect. Evidence: the diff of this file shows only insertions.

`--oc-overlay-scrim` is a NEW FAMILY and deliberately not an `--oc-bg-*`. The `--oc-bg-*` ramp is five surfaces back-to-front; a scrim sits above all of them and veils rather than backs. The file's own `--oc-action-*` versus `--oc-status-*` argument (`:97-107`) is the precedent: families are kept apart when they mean different things. The amendment comment says so, and says why a semibold weight was needed — ten declarations in five directories independently reached for a bare `600` because `TOKENS` offered 400/500/700 and nothing between, which is the same shape the sub-session 3 amendment recorded.

`src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css` defines both new properties, once each, inside its single `:root` block: `--oc-weight-semibold: 600;` in the existing weights group (`:138-140` at `41f274e`) so the ramp reads 400/500/600/700 in order, and `--oc-overlay-scrim: color-mix(in srgb, var(--oc-bg-app) 70%, transparent);`. Positioning within `tokens.css` follows that file's existing practice of grouping by family rather than appending. Evidence: `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.test.ts` passes — it asserts both directions of the `TOKENS` <-> `tokens.css` agreement, exactly one `:root` block, and no `!important`, so a token added to one file and not the other fails it.

The overlay value INTRODUCES NO NEW COLOUR LITERAL. It derives its hue from `--oc-bg-app` through `color-mix` and adds only the alpha, which answers the exact objection the code recorded at `beachcomber/BeachcomberPreviewDialog.module.css:8-10` — `the token set has no alpha layer, and inventing one would be a color literal`. Evidence: `grep -n "#[0-9a-fA-F]\{3,8\}" src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css | wc -l` returns the same count as at startRef. The alpha must be strictly between 0 and 1: an opaque scrim would reproduce the defect, and a fully transparent one would not veil.

All TEN bare `font-weight: 600` declarations become `font-weight: var(--oc-weight-semibold)`, at these selectors and nowhere else: `.railHeading` (`lanes/LaneRail.module.css:24`), `.agentType` (`:162`), `.heading` (`pods/DeletePodDialog.module.css:34`), `.subject` (`:42`), `.heading` (`pods/NewPodDialog.module.css:36`), `.bypassWarning` (`:143`), `.heading` (`shell/EmptyWorkspace.module.css:15`), `.paneTitle` (`transcript/Transcript.module.css:85`), `.dispatchCount` (`:318`), `.dispatchAgentType` (`:356`) — line numbers as at `41f274e`. All ten are headings or emphatic labels, which is why one token serves them. Evidence, both directions: `grep -rn "font-weight: *600" src/renderer --include="*.module.css"` exits 1 with no match, positive-controlled by `grep -rno "font-weight: *var(--oc-weight-semibold)" src/renderer --include="*.module.css" | wc -l` printing exactly `10`. The first command prints 10 matches at startRef.

All FIVE remaining bare `font-weight` declarations become their EXISTING tokens, so that no `*.module.css` sets `font-weight` to a literal anywhere: `lanes/LaneRail.module.css:177`, `pods/PodBar.module.css:187` and `:208`, and `transcript/Transcript.module.css:180` take `var(--oc-weight-bold)`; `transcript/Transcript.module.css:92` takes `var(--oc-weight-regular)` — line numbers as at `41f274e`. THIS CHANGES ZERO PIXELS: `tokens.css:138-140` already defines `--oc-weight-regular: 400` and `--oc-weight-bold: 700`, so each edit is a literal-to-token swap with an identical computed value. These five are a DIFFERENT defect from the ten `600`s — bare literals whose tokens already existed — and they were folded into this task by explicit user decision at Gate 2, so that criterion 12's census can be the universal rule rather than one scoped to a single value. Evidence, both directions: `grep -rno "font-weight: *[0-9]\{3\}" src/renderer --include="*.module.css"` exits 1 with no match after the change, and printed `15` at `41f274e`; positive-controlled by `grep -rnoc "font-weight: *var(--oc-weight" src/renderer --include="*.module.css"` summing to exactly `40` — the 25 declarations already tokenised at `41f274e` plus the 15 converted by this task. No bare `font-weight` keyword values exist to convert: the census found 400/600/700 numerics only.

All FOUR full-window scrims take the overlay token, so a dialog veils the window instead of hiding it: `.confirmScrim` (`helm/Helm.module.css:413-420`, consumed by `helm/HelmCloseConfirm.tsx:90`), `.scrim` (`pods/DeletePodDialog.module.css:6-14`), `.scrim` (`pods/NewPodDialog.module.css:1-9`) and `.scrim` (`beachcomber/BeachcomberPreviewDialog.module.css:13-21`) each declare `background: var(--oc-overlay-scrim)`, replacing `background: var(--oc-bg-app)`. Each is `position: fixed; inset: 0`, so each covers the whole window and not merely the panel behind it. Evidence: `grep -rno "var(--oc-overlay-scrim)" src/renderer --include="*.module.css" | wc -l` prints exactly `4`, one occurrence in each of those four files.

PRESERVED BEHAVIOUR — stated as such and therefore exempt from the vacuity rule. The SEVEN other `--oc-bg-app` consumers in CSS are legitimate app-background surfaces and must not change: `shell/WorkspaceLayout.module.css:12`, `styles/global.css:29`, `shell/PanelRegion.module.css:16`, `transcript/Transcript.module.css:14`, `composer/Composer.module.css:49`, and `beachcomber/Beachcomber.module.css:25` and `:226`. Evidence: `grep -rno "var(--oc-bg-app)" src/renderer --include="*.css" | grep -v "^src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:" | wc -l` prints exactly `7` after the change, and the seven matching file:line pairs are exactly those listed. The unfiltered form printed `11` at `41f274e` and prints `8` after the change. AMENDED by escalation E5 (amendment A1): the count was frozen as the unfiltered `7`, derived as 11 minus the 4 converted scrims, without anticipating that criterion 4's MANDATED overlay value — `color-mix(in srgb, var(--oc-bg-app) 70%, transparent)` — necessarily adds an eighth occurrence at the token's own definition site, `styles/tokens.css:46`. As frozen, criteria 4 and 8 could not both hold: reaching an unfiltered 7 would require a colour literal, which criterion 4 forbids. The definition of a different token is not a CONSUMER, and this criterion's subject has always been the seven consumers it names, so the filter expresses what the criterion meant rather than relaxing it. The exclusion is narrow and named: it removes only the file that defines the token set. Only two of those seven files are in this task's ownership set, so the other five are additionally protected by the ownership rule.

The false docblock moves with the code. `beachcomber/BeachcomberPreviewDialog.module.css:8-10`'s paragraph — `The scrim is opaque rather than translucent for the same reason \`NewPodDialog.module.css\` is: the token set has no alpha layer, and inventing one would be a color literal` — becomes false the moment the token exists, and is REWRITTEN to state what is then true: the scrim veils the window from `--oc-overlay-scrim`, which carries the alpha and derives its hue from `--oc-bg-app`, so no literal was invented. Evidence: `grep -n "opaque rather than translucent" src/renderer/src/beachcomber/BeachcomberPreviewDialog.module.css` exits 1, and exits 0 at startRef. Prose that outlived the code it described is this project's single most repeated defect class, with eleven live instances on the backlog.

MANDATORY, AND IT FAILS THE SUITE IF SKIPPED. `'src/renderer/src/shell/EmptyWorkspace.module.css: font-weight: 600'` is DELETED from `PRE_TOKEN_SHELL_DECLARATIONS` in `src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts` (declared at `:631`, asserted at `:713` at `41f274e` — re-grep for both rather than trusting the line numbers; they moved twice on 2026-10-09 and the pre-C1 backlog roster still carries the stale `:628`/`:710`). That list is compared against the found offenders EXACTLY, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, so it is a two-sided pin that FAILS when the defect it pins is fixed. The list is left holding its five border entries. Evidence: `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts` passes, and the report states the failure observed when the stylesheet was fixed before the list was.

THE CRITERION IS THE ABSENCE OF ANY FALSIFIED CLAIM, not the deletion of a listed set of strings. After this task, `PRE_TOKEN_SHELL_DECLARATIONS`' docblock in `hygiene.test.ts` — and the file header — assert nothing this task's own change has made false. Broadened from an enumeration by user decision at Gate 2, because the enumerated three strings left the docblock's opening line and its ownership claim false, and prose that outlived the code it described is this project's single most repeated defect class. The KNOWN instances, all present at `41f274e`, are the known set and NOT the whole obligation: (a) the opening line `THE DECLARATIONS THIS RULE FINDS THAT THIS TASK DOES NOT FIX, EXHAUSTIVELY` — this task fixes one of them; (b) the claim that `font-weight: 600` `has NO token, since the set offers 400/500/700` — it has one now; (c) `these six` and `A seventh raw declaration`, which become five and sixth; (d) the claim that both stylesheets `live outside this task's ownership` and that fixing them `belongs to whoever owns `shell/`, with the weight decision made deliberately rather than rounded by a test author` — THIS task owns both files, fixes one, and the weight decision was made deliberately, by escalation E1; and (e) the file header's `the three \`--oc-weight-*\` keys`, which becomes four. Evidence: each of `grep -n "has NO token"`, `grep -n "A seventh raw declaration"`, `grep -n "THIS TASK DOES NOT FIX"`, `grep -n "belongs to whoever owns"` and `grep -n "the three .--oc-weight"` over that file exits 1 after the change, and each exits 0 at startRef — all five verified to match exactly once at `41f274e`, each on a single line. Do NOT substitute a phrase that spans a line break in the source: `live outside this task` looks like a quotation of that docblock but wraps after `this`, so it matches nothing and the control cannot fire. A reviewer finding any OTHER sentence in that docblock falsified by this task should treat it as in scope for this criterion.

A NEW TWO-SIDED CENSUS in `hygiene.test.ts` guards both conversions against regression, scanning EVERY `*.module.css` under `src/renderer/src` with CSS comments stripped (comments must be stripped: `permissions/PermissionCards.module.css:4` discusses `position: fixed` in prose and is not a scrim). (a) THE UNIVERSAL RULE: no declaration sets `font-weight` to anything but a `var(--oc-weight-*)` token, with NO exception list. It is universal rather than scoped to the literal `600` by user decision at Gate 2, which folded the last five literals into criterion 6 to make it available — a value-scoped rule would have guarded one value while leaving the class open, and the alternative was a NEW exception list, which is the artifact criterion 10 exists to shrink. NOTE THE SCOPE TRAP: the existing offender scan at `:642` walks only `TOKENISED_STYLE_ROOTS` (`:539-543`) — `beachcomber`, `helm` and `shell` — which is precisely why the five literals in `lanes`, `pods` and `transcript` were never offenders and never appeared in the pin. This census must walk EVERY `*.module.css` under `src/renderer/src`, and the test must assert its own file list is non-empty and names a file from a directory outside those three roots, so a census that silently scanned nothing cannot report as a pass. (b) Every rule declaring both `position: fixed` and `inset: 0` that sets a `background` sets it to `var(--oc-overlay-scrim)`, and there are EXACTLY FOUR such rules, named individually so the count cannot drift silently in either direction.

Each new matcher in the census is PROVED ABLE TO FIRE against a synthetic violation AND its clean twin, in the same file, before it is relied on — this file's own stated convention (`every matcher is proved against a synthetic sample first — a hygiene rule that cannot fire is worse than no rule`) and the test discipline's rule that a test is established only by being seen to fail. Watch the `prop:\s*(?!var\()` trap the file documents at `:575-593`: `\s*` backtracks to zero width and the lookahead then fires on a perfectly tokenised declaration. The report names the command and the observed failure of each new assertion before the stylesheets were converted.

REPO-WIDE TYPECHECK OVER BOTH PROGRAMS passes: `npm run typecheck`, which runs `typecheck:node` (`tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json --composite false`) and `typecheck:web` (`tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.web.json --composite false`) — script names read from `package.json` at `41f274e`. Vitest transpiles without typechecking, so no scoped suite in this session can catch a type error, and this session amends the theme contract. The report states the exit code of `npm run typecheck` and confirms both sub-scripts ran.

FULL SUITE ON THE QUIESCENT TREE: `npm test` (`vitest run`) reports 0 failures, at least 141 test files and at least 2233 tests — the baseline measured at `9c8ad46`. `at least` rather than `exactly` because criterion 12 adds assertions. This task is the DAG tail precisely so this number is measured on a tree no peer is still writing to: a previous session saw 8 phantom failures that were a concurrent peer mid-write. The report quotes the run's own file and test counts rather than restating the baseline.

PATH-SCOPED, because peers hold uncommitted work in this shared worktree by design and the unscoped form of this criterion is unsatisfiable here: no file outside this task's `owns` globs appears in THIS task's diff. In particular T1's three `shell/PanelBar.*` files and T2's `contracts/renderer-panels.ts`, `state/panel-store.ts` and `helm/HelmPanel.tsx` are untouched by this task. `pods/PodBar.module.css` IS owned by this task as of the Gate 2 decision and is expected in its diff, with exactly two changed lines (`:187`, `:208`).
